ulpur-zamindar-bari.desc: Ulpur, a short ride from Gopalganj town, was home to a big family of Hindu zamindars; the estate is said to have had about a hundred sharers. Around 1900 the zamindar Pritish Chandra Basu Roy Chowdhury laid out a large compound here, with a natghar (performance hall), separate houses for the brothers and a cremation ground. Many buildings have since been pulled down or taken over, but enough old brick facades, arches and courtyards remain to give a feel of the place. It falls under the Department of Archaeology's Gopalganj unit.
blocks: From Gopalganj town take an auto or CNG to Ulpur union (about 30 minutes) and ask for the jomidar bari in Moddhopara.
People live in parts of the compound, so ask before walking into courtyards. Some structures are fragile; don't climb on them.

orakandi-thakurbari.desc: In the 19th century Harichand Thakur founded the Matua movement in Orakandi, a reform faith that drew many Namasudra farmers and rejected caste discrimination. His son Guruchand Thakur promoted education and social uplift for the community. The Thakurbari in Kashiani upazila holds their temples and remains a pilgrimage centre for Matua followers in Bangladesh and India. It is lively during festivals and quiet the rest of the year.
blocks: From Gopalganj town or Kashiani, take a CNG to Orakandi.
Remove shoes where asked and ask before photographing rituals.

kashiani-rasmalai.desc: In Kashiani upazila, on the Madhumati side of Gopalganj, Kashiani Mishty Ghar on Thana Road is known for its rasmalai: chhana balls soaked in milk reduced until thick and rich. Food writers have rated it denser and milkier than most. The shop also makes rajbhog and a chomchom it has been selling for more than two decades. It is an easy stop for travellers heading to Bhatiapara or Orakandi. Ask for whatever was made that morning.

kotalipara-floating-gardens.desc: Where land stays under water for months, farmers in Kotalipara and nearby areas build floating beds called dhap or baira from rotted water hyacinth and other plants. On them they grow seedlings, gourds, okra and leafy greens, moving the beds by boat. The method has been practised for generations and is recognised by the FAO as a globally important agricultural heritage system. Seeing the green rafts spread across the water is unforgettable.
blocks: From Gopalganj town take a bus or CNG to Kotalipara, then ask for a boat to the floating beds.
Go with a local boatman and ask farmers before stepping near their beds.

gopalganj-court-mosque.desc: The Court Mosque stands in the middle of Gopalganj town, near the court area. Work on it began in 1947. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his father Sheikh Lutfar Rahman both prayed here, which is why many visitors to Tungipara stop by. It is a working town mosque rather than a monument, so keep the visit short and respectful.
blocks: Rickshaw or easy-bike from anywhere in Gopalganj town; it is in the town centre near the court area.
Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. Pair it with the Tungipara mausoleum complex, about 20 km away.

gopalganj-rasgolla.desc: Gopalganj is best known for its rasgolla, white chhana balls cooked in light syrup until soft and springy. Long-running shops in Gopalganj town have been making them for decades, and Bhatiapara's older shops are known for small rasgollas. Locals also rate the district's sandesh, doi and chhanar jilapi. Buy a hari (clay pot) of rasgolla to take home.

chanda-beel.desc: Chanda Beel is a vast low-lying wetland spreading across parts of Gopalganj and Madaripur. In the monsoon and autumn it fills with water, and boats move through fields of white and red water lilies. Villages sit on raised mounds, reachable only by boat in the wet season. It is also an important area for freshwater fish and wintering birds.
blocks: From Gopalganj town or Kotalipara, hire a CNG to a beel-edge village and then a local boat.
Hire a boat with a local guide; go early for lilies and birds.

tungipara-mausoleum.desc: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the leader of Bangladesh's independence movement, was born in Tungipara in 1920 and buried here after his assassination in 1975. The complex includes his grave under a domed memorial, his ancestral home, a library and a museum. The surrounding village sits beside the Baghiar river, with ponds and old trees. It is a major place of national history whatever one's politics.
blocks: Bus from Dhaka via the Padma Bridge to Tungipara, about 3–4 hours; or from Gopalganj town by bus or CNG.

glance: Bazaars in Gopalganj town and Kotalipara, or a village homestay
gopalganj-beel-fish.desc: Gopalganj's wetlands provide an abundance of freshwater fish. Climbing perch (koi), stinging catfish (shing), snakehead (shol) and small fish like puti and mola fill the markets after the rains. Home cooks make them into thin jhol with potato, gourd or shapla stems from the beel. Eating a home-cooked fish meal is the best way to taste the district.

orakandi-baruni-snan.desc: Around the birth anniversary of Harichand Thakur in the Bangla month of Chaitra, Orakandi hosts the Baruni Snan, a holy bath and fair. Pilgrims arrive with red and white flags, beating large danka drums and gongs and singing devotional songs. Thousands bathe in the sacred pond at Thakurbari and a big fair fills the fields for several days. It is a powerful display of a living folk faith.
blocks: Expect large crowds; respect bathing areas and rituals.
